```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(epidemiologysuite)
```

Worked examples of the sample-size functions. Each help page (for example `?calc_means_2s_indep`) lists every argument and gives the
source of the formula; the numbers below are computed when this page is built.

## One proportion, one mean

How many people are needed to estimate a prevalence of about 50% to within 5 percentage points?

```{r prop}
calc_proportion_precision(p = 0.5, d = 0.05)$n
```

## Comparing two groups

Two means: a difference of half a standard deviation, 80% power, 5% significance.

```{r means}
m <- calc_means_2s_indep(mu1 = 0, mu2 = 0.5, sd = 1)
m$n_per_group
```

Two proportions, 40% against 25%:

```{r props}
calc_proportion_2s(p1 = 0.40, p2 = 0.25)
```

Paired measurements (before and after in the same people), where `sd_diff` is the standard deviation of the differences:

```{r paired}
calc_means_paired(mean_diff = 0.5, sd_diff = 1)$n
```

## Survival

A log-rank comparison: event probabilities of 40% (experimental) and 60% (control) over follow-up give a hazard ratio of
`r round(log(1 - 0.4) / log(1 - 0.6), 2)`.

```{r logrank}
calc_logrank(pE = 0.4, pC = 0.6, hr = log(1 - 0.4) / log(1 - 0.6))
```

## Clustered data

When people are sampled or treated in clusters (villages, clinics), the sample size is inflated by the design effect
`1 + (m - 1) * rho`.

```{r cluster}
calc_cluster_deff(n_base = 200, icc = 0.05, cluster_size = 10)
```

The same logic applies when one patient contributes several correlated measurements (both eyes, several lesions). Two eye drops are
compared with both eyes of a patient on the same drop, a between-eye correlation of 0.3 and a difference of half a standard
deviation:

```{r eyes}
eyes <- calc_patient_units_between_continuous(delta = 0.5, sd = 1, icc = 0.3, units_per_patient = 2)
eyes$n_patients_per_arm
eyes$design_effect
eyes$n_patients_per_arm_if_units_independent
eyes$n_patients_per_arm_floor
```

Counting the 2 eyes as 2 independent people would suggest `r eyes$n_patients_per_arm_if_units_independent` patients per arm instead of
`r eyes$n_patients_per_arm`. And more eyes or patches per patient help less and less: however many units each patient contributes,
at least `r eyes$n_patients_per_arm_floor` patients per arm are needed at this correlation. With only 30 patients per arm available,
how many units per patient would be needed?

```{r units}
calc_patient_units_needed("between_continuous", patients = 30, delta = 0.5, sd = 1, icc = 0.3)[c("achievable", "n_units_per_patient")]
```

If each patient receives both treatments (one eye on each drug, the two halves of the face) the patient's own level cancels out and far
fewer patients are needed:

```{r split}
calc_patient_units_within_continuous(delta = 0.5, sd = 1, icc = 0.3, units_per_arm = 1)$n_patients
```

## Allowing for loss to follow-up

Inflate a sample size for expected loss with the attrition functions (`?calc_attrition_stages`, `?calc_attrition_arms`).
